definition: Post-Training Quantization converts a finished model (calibration only, no retraining): GPTQ, AWQ, and round-to-nearest schemes.
details: Post-Training Quantization converts a finished model (calibration only, no retraining): GPTQ, AWQ, and round-to-nearest schemes. Quantization-Aware Training simulates low precision during training for better accuracy at aggressive bit widths. PTQ dominates LLM practice for its convenience.

explainer.lead: The two main routes to lower-precision models: PTQ compresses a finished model without retraining, while QAT simulates low precision during training for better accuracy. It matters because the choice trades convenience against accuracy at aggressive bit widths.

tiers.eli5: PTQ is shrinking a finished photo to save space; QAT is practicing at low resolution the whole time so the result looks better.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers favor PTQ (GPTQ, AWQ, round-to-nearest with calibration) for LLMs because it is convenient; the pitfall is accuracy loss when pushing to very low bit widths, where QAT is preferred.
tiers.paperLevel: PTQ applies calibration only, with no retraining; QAT simulates low precision during training. No formula is specified beyond these characterizations.

explainer.example: A team quantizes a trained LLM with GPTQ using a calibration set; if accuracy degrades too much at low bits, they switch to QAT.
